q-40413.name: Question 1
q-40413.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Find the orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}.$
q-40413.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{span}\{b\}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{b\cdot a}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{2\cdot (-5)+(-2)\cdot 1+2\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{-10-2-6+2}{4+4+4+4}b \\  & =\frac{-16}{16}b \\  & =-b \\  & =-1[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-39708.name: Question 2
q-39708.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Find the orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}.$
q-39708.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{b\cdot a}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 3+0\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 3}{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{6+0+6+6}{4+0+4+4}b \\  & =\frac{18}{12}b \\  & =\frac{3}{2}b \\  & =\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-81124.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}.$
q-81124.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{b\cdot a}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 2+1\cdot 2+0\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 5}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{2+2+0+5}{1+1+0+1}b \\  & =\frac{9}{3}b \\  & =3b \\  & =3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-39727.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}.$
q-39727.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $a$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{b\cdot a}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 1+2\cdot 2+(-3)\cdot (-3)+1\cdot 4}{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{4+4+9+4}{16+4+9+1}b \\  & =\frac{21}{30}b \\  & =\frac{7}{10}b \\  & =\frac{7}{10}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{14}{5} \\ \frac{7}{5} \\ -\frac{21}{10} \\ \frac{7}{10}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-39730.problem: Let $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $a=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$ Find the orthogonal projection of $b$ onto $\text{Span}\{a\}.$
q-39730.worked_solution:
The vector projection of $b$ onto $\text{Span}\{a\}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{a\cdot b}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 2+2\cdot 4+(-2)\cdot (-4)+6\cdot 2}{{6}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{6}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{12+8+8+12}{36+4+4+36}a \\  & =\frac{40}{80}a \\  & =\frac{1}{2}a \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-40410.name: Question 6
q-40410.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Find the distance between $x$ and $\text{Span}\{b\}.$
q-40410.worked_solution:
The distance between the vector $x$ and the vector space $\text{Span}\{b\}$ is given by $‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖$, where $\overset{^}{x}$ in the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{span}\{b\}.$

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{b\cdot x}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 4+4\cdot 5+0\cdot 1+2\cdot 4}{{2}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{8+20+0+8}{4+16+0+4}b \\  & =\frac{3}{2}b \\  & =\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(4-3)^{2}+(5-6)^{2}+(1-0)^{2}+(4-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{a\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x & =\frac{a\cdot x}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 6+3\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot (-3)+1\cdot 6}{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{6+9+9+6}{1+9+9+1}a \\  & =\frac{30}{20}a \\  & =\frac{3}{2}a \\  & =\frac{3}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{9}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the following:  

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{9}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ z & =x-{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{9}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Notice that $y\in \text{Span}\{a\}$ and $z⊥\text{Span}\{a\},$ as shown in the picture above.

In conclusion, $z=[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{2} \\ -\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}].$

q-39711.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the distance between $x$ and $\text{Span}\{b\}.$
q-39711.worked_solution:
The distance between the vector $x$ and the vector space $\text{Span}\{b\}$ is given by $‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖$, where $\overset{^}{x}$ in the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{span}\{b\}.$

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{b\}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{b\cdot x}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 4+2\cdot 4+(-2)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 4}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{4+8+4+4}{1+4+4+1}b \\  & =\frac{20}{10}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}+({x}_{4}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(4-2)^{2}+(4-4)^{2}+(-2-(-4))^{2}+(4-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+0+4+4} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

q-140118.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
q-140118.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{(-4)\cdot (-3)+8\cdot 1}{{(-3)}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{20}{10}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-81199.name: Question 13
q-81199.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=0 \\ -{x}_{1}+\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
q-81199.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ -1 & \frac{1}{2} & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{4\cdot \frac{1}{2}+3\cdot 1}{{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{5}{\frac{1}{4}+1}b \\  & =4b \\  & =4[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

q-140119.name: Question 14
q-140119.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
q-140119.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are $2$ pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}$ and from the second equation ${x}_{2}=-3{x}_{3}.$  

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ -3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 1+(-5)\cdot (-3)+4\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{22}{11}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

q-81194.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=0\end{aligned}
$$
q-81194.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 2 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-2{x}_{2}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 2+2\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{10}{5}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
